author: TEDx Talks
description:
Colleen Pimentel challenges the idea that moving faster always means making progress. Her talk introduces the power of a “Strategic Pause,” encouraging audiences to step back, gain clarity, and ensure that the momentum we build is moving us in the right direction. Meet Colleen Pimentel, a Founder, Author, and GTM Business Leader with three decades of experience at tech giants like Google and Oracle. She is a leading advocate for "The Great Unlearning"—the process of trading external expectations for an authentic life defined by purpose rather than just achievement. This mission led her to a niche in transformational leadership, helping high-achievers navigate the "Fog" to reclaim their agency and fulfillment.

Throughout her 30-year career, Colleen mastered the art of reinvention, navigating over ten pivots while mentoring others to unlock their most purposeful professional chapters. Her battle-tested resilience inspired her book, Second Act, where she rewrites the rules of power and
title: The momentum trap—and how to avoid it | Colleen Pimentel | TEDxMcMasterU

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Teesha shares her personal journey of living with ADHD and how taking up long-distance running helped her channel restless energy into clarity and discipline. She emphasizes breaking big goals into small steps, letting go of perfectionism, and finding strength in showing up authentically. Teesha, studying Data Diagnostics and Digital Health, is a passionate advocate for resilience, self-acceptance, and personal growth, using her journey with ADHD and running to inspire others.
Through fitness, she has redefined discipline and perseverance, proving that progress is built one step at a time. By embracing movement as a tool for clarity and confidence, she challenges the idea of perfection and encourages people to show up for themselves, despite obstacles. Her story is a testament to the power of authenticity, small consistent actions, and the courage to step outside societal expectations to create a path of one's own. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format bu
title: Running towards a life I love | Teesha Roy | TEDxWarwick Salon

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Sahith Rajkumar challenges traditional ideas of progress by exploring the impact of consistently showing up for others. Drawing on his experiences in community outreach, he discusses how meaningful impact is not always defined by rapid or visible change, but by the commitment to stay engaged, especially when progress is uncertain. Sahith Rajkumar is an Honours Biochemistry student at McMaster University, researcher, and community advocate who challenges how we define progress. Through his work with Gore Park Community Outreach and Smiling Pillars, an initiative he founded to foster resilience and intergenerational connection, Sahith has spent over four years showing up consistently for communities in Hamilton.

His research in Indigenous health and HIV equity, combined with his sustained community work, has led him to question the metrics we use to measure impact. While progress is often celebrated as fast, visible, and upward, Sahith invites us to recognize another kind of momentum:
title: When Showing Up Is the Progress | Sahith Rajkumar | TEDxMcMasterU

description:
What does a rising subway fare tell us about fairness, justice, and systems we take for granted? 
Ryan takes us on a philosophical adventure through the economics of metro systems, contrasting government-subsidized networks like Shanghai Metro with profit-driven models, like Hong Kong’s MTR. 
This talk ultimately concerns the balance of justice between the common good and market efficiency, asking us to reflect on whether everyday services should prioritize accessibility or self-sufficiency—and what that says about the kind of world we want to live in. Youth Public Affairs Observer

description:

author: TEDx Talks
description:
كم يمكن أن تكلّفك غلطة واحدة في عالم الأعمال؟

قد تكون الفكرة رائعة، والحماس في أعلى مستوياته، والطموح بلا حدود… ومع ذلك، قد تخسر سنوات من العمل بسبب قرار واحد لم تستعد له جيدًا.

في هذا الحديث، يشارك إبراهيم أنور خلاصة رحلة امتدت لأكثر من 15 عامًا في عالم الأعمال، والاستشارات والعمل مع أكثر من 100 شركة، مستعرضًا مجموعة من الدروس التي تحولت مع الوقت إلى ما يصفه بـ «30 رصاصة لحماية حياتك المهنية».

من معرفة نقاط قوتك واختيار الفريق المناسب، إلى أهمية توثيق الاتفاقات، وبناء رؤية واضحة، وإدارة المال، والتميّز عن المنافسين، والتفاوض، والتعامل مع الفشل، وبناء العلاقات، وصولًا إلى الحفاظ على نفسك من الاحتراق المهني.

كل «رصاصة» في هذا الحديث وُلدت من تجربة حقيقية؛ من خسارة، أو خطأ، أو قرار، أو درس لم يكن من السهل تعلّمه.

ففي عالم الأعمال، لا يكفي أن تعرف كيف تنجح…
بل تحتاج أيضًا إلى أن تعرف كيف تحمي نفسك من الأخطاء التي قد تمنعك من الوصول.

هذا الحديث ليس وصفة للنجاح، بل مجموعة من الدروس التي كان يتمنى إبراهيم أن يعرفها قبل أن يبدأ.

فإذا كنت في بداية طريقك المهني، أو تبني مشروعك، أو تبحث
title: ٣٠ رصاصة لحماية حياتك المهنية | Ebrahem Anwar | TEDxYouth@TabaryElHegazHS

author: TEDx Talks
description:
在主流叙事中，麻风病康复者常被标签化为可怕的传染者、需要救助的弱者，或是苦难的化身。但如果我们的镜头只聚焦于他们的伤痛，就真的看见了他们的人生吗？
何纪文，这位麻风病康复者，用一台普通的数码相机讲述了另一种人生。他的镜头定格的不只是苦难，而是村庄的风景、村民之间温暖的合作，甚至是阳光下盛开的桃花与歌声。从“被记录的对象”到“自己的叙述者”，他用行动夺回了叙事的权利，证明每个人都能决定，什么才是生命中真正值得被看见的部分。
本场演讲中，康复村志愿者翁洁云探讨了一个深刻的问题：当我们只以同情和标签看待受苦者时，是否无意间剥夺了他们作为一个完整“人”的权利？或许，重新看见他们，也是在重新审视我们自己。 JIA工作营康复村对话项目负责人
中央民族大学人类学硕士 This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: 用镜头夺回叙事权：谁来决定，我们的人生里什么值得被看见？ | 洁云 翁 | TEDxNanshan Salon

大分県内のTOP高校に通う倉迫は、高校3年生の夏に、イタリアへ留学した。
本来であれば受験生である時期に、なぜ、彼は留学を決意したのか。
そういった難しい決断をする時の指針として、彼はいつも「妄想」をしている。
妄想が前に進んでいくパワーになっていることを、体験を通して語る。


KURASAKO Atsushi : Visualizing the "Cool Me": Turning Imagination into the Power to Move Forward


While most high school seniors in Japan were buried in textbooks, Kurasako, a student at a top school in Oita, chose a different path: Italy. 
Why did he decide to study abroad during the most critical year of his academic journey? 
The secret lies in his unique guiding principle — "visualizing the cool Me" In this video, he shares how the power of imagination can become the ultimate fuel for taking bold steps in life.


 He has accumulated diverse experiences such as classical ballet, musical theater, piano, track and field, and literary club activities for years. He has been learning vocal music since he was 8 and came in third in the national competition.

He sang the national anthems alone in public at the Oita Pre

description: L.V. Navneeth, CEO of The Hindu Group, shares his leadership philosophy that "knowing precedes doing". Drawing from over 27 years of diverse professional experience, he outlines four distinct objectives for knowing people to build a future-ready organization. Through engaging "creative experiments" , like bringing down corporate silos by changing how coffee is served, making fame a team sport to attract talent, and handwriting thousands of birthday cards; he demonstrates how fleeting moments of connection can create a lasting, systemic impact. L.V. Navaneeth serves as the Chief Executive Officer of The Hindu Group, one of India's most respected media houses with a 147-year legacy. He has accumulated over 27 years of working experience across multiple industries and geographies, including executive leadership roles in India and Indonesia. author: TEDx Talks
description:
What happens when we give AI the power to make decisions, but forget to ask whether it should be making them in the first place?

As artificial intelligence moves beyond answering questions and begins recommending, approving and acting on our behalf, the conversation around AI needs to move beyond how intelligent it is. Hemang Upadhyay explores a more important question: has AI earned the right to act?

Drawing from over 16 years of experience in technology, digital products and AI, Hemang examines what happens when automated systems operate with incomplete information, unclear boundaries or no clear path to challenge their decisions. He argues that automating a bad decision does not fix it. It simply allows the decision to travel faster.

The talk presents five principles for building AI that deserves trust: evidence, authority, visibility, restraint and recovery. Together, they offer a practical way to think about responsible AI without treating innovation and human judgment as oppo
title: Has AI Earned the Right to Act? | Hemang Upadhyay | TEDxWisdom World School Amanora

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if some of life's most useful lessons are already hidden in just a few lines of poetry?

In a world filled with self-help books, step-by-step frameworks and endless advice on how to live better, Vijay Sharma takes us somewhere much simpler: Urdu shayari and poetry.

Through timeless verses and the wisdom of poets, this talk explores how a few carefully chosen words can help us understand happiness, pain, desire, uncertainty and the challenges we experience in everyday life. Sometimes, we don't need another framework or another list of things to fix. Sometimes, we simply need words that help us pause, acknowledge what we are feeling and see it differently.

Vijay draws attention to the enduring power of poetry as a form of wisdom that does not require a subscription, an update or a step-by-step manual. A couple of lines can stay with us, travel with us and offer perspective whenever we need it.

As the next generation grows up surrounded by increasingly complex information and ins
title: What Poetry Can Teach Us About Life | Vijay S | TEDxWisdom World School Amanora

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if the beliefs limiting our future were never truly ours to begin with?

From the language we speak to the expectations we grow up with, we absorb countless beliefs from our families, communities and surroundings. Over time, these beliefs can quietly shape how we see success, opportunity and even our own potential.

In this talk, Mitu Samar Jha explores a powerful idea: the facts of our lives do not define our future. The conclusions we draw from those facts do.

Drawing from more than two decades of leadership experience and her journey from a small town in Bihar to senior leadership roles and a 25-year career, Mitu shows how the same situation can lead different people to completely different conclusions. A missed promotion can become proof that we are not capable, or it can become a reason to learn and try again. Being uncomfortable in a room can become a reason to stay silent, or an opportunity to make ourselves heard.

Her message goes beyond positive thinking. She argues th
title: What If Your Limiting Beliefs Aren't Yours? | Mitu Samarnath Jha | TEDxWisdom World School Amanora

description:
When it comes to animal adoption, even the kindest intentions can make it difficult to let go of the mindset of being a “savior.” In her talk, Xia Liu invites us to rethink this idea: perhaps the one truly transformed by adoption is ourselves.
From rescuing a disabled puppy named Kangaroo to founding Qingdao Adoption Day, she has spent 15 years showing that changing the fate of stray animals is never the work of a few heroes, but the result of countless ordinary people choosing to pause, show kindness, and take action. Love doesn’t have to feel heavy—it can be warm, joyful, and part of everyday life.
在谈论动物领养时，即便出于完全的善心，我们也总是很难在心理上摆脱“救世主”的身份。但刘霞在这场演讲中希望观众重新思考：或许领养真正被改变的，是我们自己。
从救助残疾小狗“袋鼠”，到创办青岛领养日，她用十五年实践证明，改变流浪动物命运的从来不是少数英雄，而是无数普通人的一次停留、一份善意、一个行动。爱不必沉重，它也可以温暖、时尚，并融入每个人的日常。
 Founder of Qingdao Adoption Day and initiator of Qingdao’s first stray animal rescue and adoption team.
Her connection with stray animals began 15 years ago. Since 2011, she has been on the way of promoting Qingdao
title: The Smallest Act of Heroism 最小的英雄主义 | Xia Liu | TEDxNew Channel Qingdao

Ultimately, she argues that our circumstances and labels may shape our story, but our choices determine who we become. description: Adham didn’t really have a plan when he chose a college major he knew nothing about. He just went with it. Along the way, he found his way back to something he had loved since childhood: cooking. Today, he has sponsors, supports himself, and shows how following what you love can take you places you never expected. Adham is a science student and home cook who started filming his own recipes, from Egyptian dishes to comfort food classics, and grew it into a following of over 2 million across social media. Still just “a young cook” at heart, his story shows that passion and consistency can turn an everyday hobby into real impact. description:
Hay historias que aprendimos en la escuela… y otras que, simplemente, nunca nos contaron.
Durante mucho tiempo, creímos que algunos pueblos pertenecían únicamente al pasado. Pero hay personas que se dedican a demostrar que la memoria sigue viva cuando alguien decide escucharla, investigarla y compartirla.

Una propuesta de volver a los orígenes, no para mirar el pasado con nostalgia, sino para comprender cuánto de ese pasado sigue viviendo en nosotros.
 Historiador, miembro del Pueblo Camiare (Comechingón) y un prolífico
autor con tres libros publicados en historia y literatura. Es docente, investigador del Centro de Investigaciones del Instituto de Culturas Aborígenes y responsable de la Colección Indígena "Mafalda Tapia" (Editorial UPC). Su labor transmedia incluye el proyecto Los
Fuegos de Sitón y el ciclo audiovisual Te cuento otra historia. En la muestra "Un pueblo de indios", participó con su texto poético en el Museo Ferreyra y luego como coautor en el Centro Cultural de la UNC

description:
What if we stopped judging government by what it shows us—and started judging it by what ordinary people experience every day?

For Nigerian political satirist Arua Kevin Chinedu, professionally known as Kevinblak, satire is more than comedy.

It is memory refusing to remain silent.

In this powerful and deeply personal talk, Kevin takes us beyond his famous fictional character, Governor Amuneke, to the real experiences that created him. Growing up in a small community in Enugu State, Kevin witnessed what government could look like when it worked: public schools people were proud of, a functioning health centre, and pipe-borne water that flowed because one local leader decided to solve a problem.

Then, slowly, those things disappeared.
The taps stopped flowing.
The schools deteriorated.

The health centre became silent.
And something even more dangerous happened.

People adjusted.

They complained. Then they adapted. Then they normalized it.

title: What Happens When Citizens Stop Expecting Better? | Kevin Arua (Governor Amuneke) | TEDxMaitama

description:
In speaker Huyen "Julia" Nguyen's talk, titled “From Ego to Belonging: When Dreams Learn to Breathe,” she reflects upon going from being focused on yourself to finding something bigger to care about. Her talk is about realising you don’t grow by doing everything alone, but by connecting with people, finding where you belong, and still being yourself.
 Huyen Nguyen (Julia) is a Communications Officer at the Research and Training Centre for Community Development (RTCCD) in Hanoi, where she works on public health advocacy and social projects. With a background in International Relations, she has represented Vietnam in several international youth programs, workshops, and community projects focused on public health and development, bringing together policy, education, and young people’s voices.

title: From Ego to Belonging: When Dreams Learn to Breathe | Huyen Nguyen | TEDxISPH Youth

description:
Driven by a strong interest in both technology and education, speaker Duc Minh looks beyond traditional methods and asks a simple but powerful question: how can learning be made not just effective, but genuinely engaging?

In his talk, titled “Gamification,” he explores how elements of game design can be applied to everyday learning where we transform passive experiences into ones that are interactive, motivating, and meaningful.
 Hey, I’m Duc Minh. I’m a student at Posts and Telecommunications Institute of Technology (PTIT) and a part of the organising team for many student-led events related to English in PTIT. As a speaker for TEDxISPH 2026, I hope to bring a newer and more practical perspective, drawn from my interests in technology and education, to many people by showing that ideas change everything. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Gamification | Duc Minh Nguyen | TEDxISPH Youth
